title: Quantum Foundations
description: Develop quantum theory from physical principles, compare alternative theories, and explore measurement, contextuality, entanglement, dynamics, and open systems.
details: 17 draft chapters · Exercises with hints and worked solutions
prerequisite: Comfort with vectors, matrices, and probability at the level of a first university course. No prior quantum mechanics required.
summary: Derive quantum theory from physical principles and examine what its assumptions mean.

title: Quantum Information Theory
description: An advanced course on distinguishability, channels, entropy inequalities, entanglement, compression, communication, recovery, and resource theories.
details: 10 draft chapters · 100 exercises with hints and worked solutions · Research practicum
prerequisite: Quantum Foundations and introductory Quantum Information, or equivalent knowledge of density operators, tensor products, measurements, and entropy. Comfort with linear algebra and probability.
summary: Derive operational bounds and study the limits of quantum communication and resources.

title: Quantum Error Correction
description: Protect unknown quantum states using stabilizer and CSS codes, decode syndromes, contain circuit faults, and estimate the resources for reliable quantum computation.
details: 10 draft chapters · 100 solved exercises · Verified code and circuit examples
prerequisite: Quantum Information Theory and basic Quantum Computing, or equivalent knowledge of states, channels, Pauli operators, reference systems, and circuits. Binary coding theory is introduced in context.
summary: Construct quantum codes and carry their protection through noisy computations.

title: Quantum Cryptography
description: Derive quantum cryptographic security from states and adversaries through BB84, entanglement, entropy bounds, reconciliation, universal hashing, decoy states, and cryptographic limitations.
details: 6 developed draft chapters · 60 solved exercises · Reproducible Python laboratory · Protocol audit project
prerequisite: Quantum Information or equivalent knowledge of qubits, measurement, tensor products, and elementary probability. No prior cryptography required.
summary: Turn quantum signals into secret keys and examine the assumptions behind security.

title: Interpretations of Quantum Mechanics
description: Examine the measurement problem, decoherence, Bell and contextuality constraints, and competing accounts of states, outcomes, and probability through mathematical examples.
details: 10 draft chapters · 100 exercises with hints and worked solutions · Comparative research practicum
prerequisite: Quantum Foundations or equivalent knowledge of states, density operators, tensor products, measurement, and probability. Quantum Information Theory is helpful; elementary calculus is used for Bohmian dynamics.
summary: Compare interpretations through shared experiments, explicit assumptions, and mathematical arguments.

title: Quantum Experiments
description: Explore laboratory and thought experiments from single-particle interference to Wigner’s friend, with animated models, explicit assumptions, and quantitative investigations.
details: 24 developed chapters · 24 interactive models · 72 solved problems · Synthetic-data capstone
prerequisite: Basic algebra, waves, and probability. Vectors and quantum notation are introduced through examples; later chapters use simple matrices and tensor products.
summary: Connect quantum laboratory and thought experiments to predictions, measurements, and evidence.

title: Quantum Computing
description: From logic and reversible computation to quantum states, interference, circuits, and algorithms. Develop the mathematical foundations and explore them through interactive experiments.
prerequisite: Basic linear algebra. No prior quantum mechanics required.
summary: Build from classical computation to quantum states, circuits, and algorithms.

title: Quantum Algorithms
description: Develop quantum algorithms through coherent computation, phase encoding, Fourier methods, amplitude manipulation, walks, and operator transformations.
details: 11 developed chapters · Worked examples and solved problems · By Mithilesh Kumar
prerequisite: Quantum Computing course or equivalent knowledge.
summary: Explore the techniques behind interference, quantum search, and simulation.

title: Quantum Programming
description: Turn quantum algorithms into correct, testable, and reproducible programs with Qiskit. Explore language design, circuit construction, simulation, compilation, and hardware execution.
details: 16 developed chapters · Worked examples and solved problems · By Mithilesh Kumar
prerequisite: Quantum Computing and Quantum Algorithms, or equivalent knowledge. Python essentials are introduced in the course.
summary: Turn quantum algorithms into testable, reproducible programs with Qiskit.

title: Quantum Information
description: From distinguishable messages and classical information to quantum states, entanglement, compression, error correction, communication, and cryptography. Develop the necessary mathematics through concrete information-processing tasks.
details: 16 developed chapters · Worked examples and solved problems · By Mithilesh Kumar
prerequisite: No prior quantum mechanics, information theory, or linear algebra course required. Mathematics is developed in context.
summary: Study quantum states, entanglement, and the limits of communication.

title: Quantum Hardware
description: From physical qubits, control, coupling, and readout to hardware platforms, bosonic and topological encodings, processor architecture, and fault-tolerant implementation.
details: 19 developed chapters · Worked examples and solved problems · By Mithilesh Kumar
prerequisite: Quantum Computing course or equivalent knowledge. Device physics is introduced in context.
summary: Connect qubits and gates to physical devices and quantum processors.
